# Venue record: NeurIPS 2026, Main Track

Record of what the venue requires and how its accepted papers are written, for the other roles to consult.
Source of the requirements: the world's venue library (`ht-role venue neurips`, retrieved by it 2026-11-14 from
neurips.cc, the Main Track Handbook, the Reviewer Guidelines, the OpenReview invitation and the style kit).
Each statement is marked **[venue]** (stated by the venue's own source), **[derived]** (measured by me from the
sample of accepted papers below) or **[recommendation]** (my budget or advice; not a venue rule).
The files of the official kit are in `template/` (`ht-role venue neurips --template DIR` copies them).

## 1. Choice of venue and edition

**NeurIPS 2026 (40th NeurIPS), Main Track, single-column.** Edition: NeurIPS 2026 is the newest NeurIPS edition with a
published call for papers; the 2027 pages return HTTP 404 on 2026-11-14 **[venue]**. Its submission deadline (6 May 2026)
has passed, so this is a format and standard to write to, not a live submission. The delivery is never submitted by any role.

Why this one among the three allowed (reasons are mine; the objective leaves the choice open):
- The objective asks for a venue checklist "such as the NeurIPS paper checklist": NeurIPS has one, mandatory, 16 items,
  inside the single PDF and outside the page limit. ICML 2027 has an Impact Statement and AI Disclosure Statement instead;
  ICLR 2027 has an AI-use statement and optional reproducibility statement. NeurIPS's checklist questions
  (statistical significance, compute, assets and licences, limitations, theory assumptions) are the objective's review
  criteria almost verbatim, so the checklist is a free audit for this study.
- 9 content pages in **one column**, 5.5 in text width, against ICML's 8 two-column pages: the outline carries five or six
  figures, a derivation summary and an experiments section; a one-column page holds this better.
- Reviewers score Quality, Clarity, Significance, Originality, and the venue says "originality does not necessarily
  require introducing an entirely new method" and that Negative Results are accepted (at a higher bar).
  This fits a study whose contribution is a protocol, a verified law and an honest comparison.
- ICLR 2027 is under review now with unpublished score fields ("could not be established"), which makes it the weakest
  standard to write against.

If another role needs a different choice, say so in an issue here with the reason; the template, limits and the budget
below then change together.

## 2. Page limit and length **[venue]**

- Main text: **nine content pages including all figures and tables**. Not counted: references, technical appendices,
  the paper checklist, acknowledgments. Over the limit: "will not be reviewed". Camera-ready only: a tenth page.
- References, appendices, checklist: no limit. The whole upload is one PDF, at most 50 MB. The appendix goes in the same PDF
  after the references ("do not upload a separate PDF file for the appendix"); the paper must stand alone without it.
- Suggested order of the single PDF: main text, references, appendix, checklist.
- Reviewers are not required to read the appendix or supplement: **a claim the main text relies on has to be shown in the
  nine pages.** Evidence that is critical (Fig. 2, the primary comparison, the validity of the theory) must not be left to the appendix.

I moved the paper onto the NeurIPS 2026 template and answered `venue-repo`'s request (#3), which I closed. The paper still has no results text: the abstract and introduction are placeholders and I haven't drafted the method, theory or experiments yet. Those wait on `experiment-repo`'s code and numbers.

- **Template:** `paper/main.tex` now uses the unmodified `neurips_2026.sty` in submission mode, with an appendix file and the checklist loaded after the references. I removed the checklist's instruction block and kept its heading. The checklist answers are still template placeholders and must be filled in before any version is offered.
- **Build:** I built it locally with the document command; it succeeds and produces 9 pages. That count is only the placeholder text. I haven't confirmed that the system's own build passes.
- **Split:** I dropped the `venue/` line from `.forgejo/CODEOWNERS`, since the template files now sit in `paper/`. The README matches.
- **Reply to venue:** I gave `venue-repo` the delivered paths. These are `paper/main.tex` and `paper/checklist.tex` for the source and checklist, `paper/main.pdf` for the built PDF, `code/` and `code/README.md` for the code and reproduction notes, and `results/` for the reported numbers.
- **Code ZIP:** the anonymised ZIP is not a committed path; it gets cut from `code/` for the release.
